title: Robinhood Chain's real-world assets jump fivefold as tokenized stocks start trading in bigger size
dek: Real-world assets on Robinhood Chain surged to approximately $70 million, a fivefold increase in less than two weeks, with a dozen tokenized stocks each clearing at least $500,000 in daily volume as of mid-to-late July 2026. Tokenized GameStop, Nvidia, and SpaceX are generating millions in daily volume. Despite the RWA surge, memecoins and stablecoins still dominate the chain's total trading activity.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Robinhood Chain's tokenized real-world assets reached $70 million in value, with a dozen tokenized stocks each clearing at least $500,000 in daily volume.
bottom_line: Watch whether daily volumes in tokenized stocks hold above $500,000 per asset and grow as a fraction of total chain activity. The premise breaks if memecoins and stablecoins reclaim the top trending slots, or if individual tokenized equity volume drops materially over the next two weeks.
body: Real-world assets on Robinhood Chain surged to approximately $70 million in value, a roughly fivefold increase in less than two weeks, according to CoinDesk reporting. The surge marks the first material move toward the blockchain's stated purpose: tokenized equities trading at institutional scale.

A dozen tokenized stocks are now each clearing at least $500,000 in daily volume, with several surpassing $1 million. Tokenized GameStop is doing $26.6 million in daily volume on the exchange. Tokenized Nvidia is doing $14 million in daily volume. Tokenized SpaceX is doing $6.4 million in daily volume.

The real-world asset value increased from the low tens of millions of dollars, which represented just 4 percent of the network at its prior level. Total value locked on Robinhood Chain has roughly tripled since mid-July to about $312 million according to DefiLlama, and the chain is now clearing more than $600 million in daily decentralized exchange volume. Over 30 days, Robinhood Chain has recorded more than 138 million transactions per Token Terminal.

The tokenized stocks generate roughly $55 million in daily volume, under a tenth of the chain's nearly $600 million in total DEX trading. This gap underscores a persistent structural reality: memecoins, such as CASHCAT, and stablecoins still dominate the chain's activity. In Robinhood Chain's earliest days, CASHCAT, a memecoin built around Robinhood's abandoned original name, was its busiest market. After CEO Vlad Tenev followed CASHCAT's account, the token spiked more than 1,700 percent. CASHCAT is now down about 75 percent from its peak. The top of Robinhood Chain's trending list on DEX Screener is filled with tokens like Hoodrat, Vladhood, and Swole Doge, not the tokenized equities the network was built for. Stablecoins remain the single largest presence on the chain, with a combined market value in the hundreds of millions of dollars.

The surge in tokenized equity volume represents a genuine shift in the chain's transaction mix. Yet the brief trajectory of CASHCAT, from speculative mania to collapse, illustrates a deeper tension: whether institutional demand for tokenized stocks can sustain against the gravitational pull of speculation. The sources confirm that tokenized stocks still represent under a tenth of the chain's total DEX volume, and note that it will need to keep growing to meet Robinhood's original vision for tokenization.
